questions.q: The Southeast regional sales manager asks for "something simple showing how sales are doing by region and product line this quarter." What should happen next?
options: Ask follow-up questions to turn the vague request into a specific, answerable one
Start building in Power BI immediately so there's a draft to show by Monday
Write the T-SQL query first, then ask questions only if the query returns unexpected results
Tell the manager the request is too vague to act on
questions.explain: A short clarifying conversation up front prevents guessing wrong on time window, scope, metric, or grouping and finding out only after the deadline.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four things this lesson says every reporting request needs clarified before building?
options: Which cloud provider will host the Power BI workspace
The time window (e.g., which quarter, and as of when)
The scope (which regions are actually in view)
The metric(s) that answer the stakeholder's real question
questions.explain: The four things to clarify are time window, scope, metric, and grouping/audience — hosting infrastructure isn't part of requirements clarification for this project.

questions.q: Why does the lesson treat 'total sales amount AND order count' as the right metric choice here, rather than picking just one?
options: The stakeholder wants to see whether a slow quarter is fewer orders or smaller ones, which needs both numbers side by side
Power BI requires at least two measures on every report
T-SQL cannot aggregate a single column by itself
AdventureWorks2012 only stores order count, not sales amount
questions.explain: Clarifying the real question behind 'how sales are doing' revealed the manager cares about both volume and order activity, not just one number.

questions.q: What does 'grain' mean in the context of this report?
options: The level of detail the report is built at — one row per territory and product line combination
The font size used on the final Power BI dashboard
The refresh frequency of the underlying data source
The total row count returned by the T-SQL query
questions.explain: Grain describes how fine or coarse each row of the result is — here, each row represents one territory/product-line combination for the quarter.

questions.q: Which of these is explicitly scoped OUT of this project, according to the lesson?
options: A multi-year sales trend and a full data warehouse/ETL pipeline
A single T-SQL query against AdventureWorks2012
A Power BI report with a couple of DAX measures
Showing the current quarter's sales by region and product line
questions.explain: The ask was for a quick quarterly snapshot, not a historical trend or a warehouse build — matching effort to the actual request is part of scoping it correctly.
